transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. I, uh... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble lately. It's probably nothing major—I mean, I'm 68, so maybe a little of this is just normal—but... well, I keep forgetting things that I really shouldn't. 

Like, well... I've missed some heart follow-up appointments, which I know I shouldn't do, and I keep meaning to call the clinic back, but it just completely slips my mind. And even just doing little things, like if I go to do a repair job, I'll show up and realize I didn't bring the right tools with me. 

It's just a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I've always tried to be reliable. I don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill or waste your time, but... does that make sense? Am I explaining that okay?
Aside from the memory difficulties, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or losing interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Oh, no, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, sure, I get a little frustrated with myself when I mess up or forget to bring a tool with me, but... no, I'm definitely not sad or feeling down. 

I still really enjoy keeping busy and doing my projects. I try to keep a pretty positive outlook on life, honestly. I don't want you to think I'm sitting around moping or anything like that, because I'm really not. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Did these memory issues come on gradually over time, or did they seem to start suddenly?

Well, gosh, Doctor... I'm really sorry, but I'm not entirely sure how to answer that. I wish I had a better timeline for you. 

I don't think it was sudden, like waking up one morning and suddenly forgetting things... but honestly, I haven't really kept a close eye on it. I guess it might have just crept up on me? Or, well, maybe I've always been a little bit scatterbrained and it's just getting a bit more noticeable now that I'm older and have these important doctor appointments to keep track of. 

I really hope I'm not being too vague for you. I just want to give you the most accurate answer, and I'd hate to guess and steer you wrong. Is it alright if I say I just don't really know for sure?
Have these memory issues interfered with your ability to handle your everyday tasks and responsibilities independently?

Well, I... I guess they have, a little bit. I really hate to admit it, because I've always prided myself on being independent and helpful, you know? But... well, I volunteer with a repair group at the senior center, and... it's gotten to the point where they can't really count on me the way they used to. I'll forget to show up, or I'll be there but I won't have the things I need to actually do the work. 

And, like I mentioned before, my doctor's office has actually had to call and chase me down about those missed heart follow-ups. I feel just awful about making them do that, it's so disrespectful of their time. 

I'm still managing my day-to-day stuff at home alright, I think. But... I suppose it is affecting those outside things more than I'd like to admit. Does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to be honest with you.
Have you ever had a stroke, a mini-stroke, or any sudden episodes of weakness or numbness?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I've never had a stroke or a mini-stroke, or any of that sudden weakness or numbness you mentioned. 

I mean, I get the usual aches and pains of getting a bit older, maybe a stiff joint here and there, but definitely nothing scary like a stroke. My heart doctor keeps a pretty good eye on me, well, when I actually make it to the appointments, anyway. But physically, aside from the ticker, I think I'm doing pretty well! 

I hope that's the right kind of information you need? I definitely don't want to leave anything out if it's important, but I can safely say I haven't had any of those stroke symptoms.

Well, let's see... I really want to give you a good answer here. I'd say... maybe it's been causing real trouble for about a year and two months? Give or take a little bit. 

It kind of lines up with when I had that cardiac scare. After that, I had to cut way back on my walking and, you know, all those little projects that used to keep me settled and out of trouble. I guess without all that to burn off my extra energy, the forgetfulness and... well, the scatterbrained stuff just got a lot harder to manage. 

I hope a year and two months is specific enough for you? I really try not to make a fuss about these things, but I want to make sure I'm giving you the timeline you need to figure this all out. Am I doing okay with these questions?
Looking back to when you were a child or teenager, were you often scatterbrained, easily distracted, or having trouble sitting still back then as well?

Well, gosh... I suppose I was, yes. I always just tried to think of it as having a lot of spirit, you know? Boys will be boys, and all that. 

But... well, if I'm being completely honest with you, even back as a boy in grade school, I was... I was that kid who just couldn't seem to stay in his seat. I'd get so eager and I'd just blurt out the answers before the teacher even finished asking the question. And... oh, it's a little embarrassing to admit at my age, but I got quite a few notes sent home to my parents because I talked too much in class. 

I always meant well, I promise! I really wanted to be a good student and make my teachers happy, my motor just always ran a little too fast, I guess. Does that help answer your question? I hope I'm not painting too terrible a picture of myself, I really was a good-hearted kid.
Throughout your adulthood and working years, did you continue to struggle with being easily distracted, restless, or disorganized?

Well, you know, I always managed to keep a job, provided for my family. I was a hard worker, really I was. But... I suppose, if I look back honestly, I did always have a bit of a hard time keeping things perfectly organized. 

I worked in a warehouse for a long time, and I was always moving, always on my feet, which suited me just fine! But when it came to the paperwork or keeping track of the inventory logs... well, I might have misplaced a clipboard or two. And sometimes I'd get a little ahead of myself and start loading a truck before checking the final manifest. 

It wasn't that I didn't care, I just... I liked to get things done quickly. My supervisors knew I was a good egg, though. They'd just remind me to slow down a bit. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad employee? I always tried my very best to do right by them. Is that the sort of thing you're looking for?
